problem.paragraph: Explain the relationship $$-\cos^{-1}t + C = \left. \int{\frac{dt}{\sqrt{1 - t^{2}}} = \sin^{-1}t + C.} \right.$$ Is it true, in general, that $$\cos^{-1}t = -\sin^{-1}t?$$

solution.paragraph: $$cos(\pi 2-\theta )=sin\theta .cos(\pi 2-\theta )=sin\theta .$$ So, $$sin-1t=\pi 2-cos-1t.sin-1t=\pi 2-cos-1t.$$ They differ by a constant.

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, solve for the antiderivative $$\int f$$ of f with $$C = 0,$$ then use a calculator to graph f and the antiderivative over the given interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack.$$ Identify a value of C such that adding C to the antiderivative recovers the definite integral $$F(x) = {\int_{a}^{x}{f(t)dt.}}$$

solution.paragraph: The antiderivative is $$sin-1(x3)+C.sin-1(x3)+C.$$ Taking $$C=\pi 2C=\pi 2$$ recovers the definite integral.
The antiderivative is $$12tan-1(sinx2)+C.12tan-1(sinx2)+C.$$ Taking $$C=12tan-1(sin(6)2)C=12tan-1(sin(6)2)$$ recovers the definite integral.

In the following exercises, use a calculator to graph the antiderivative $$\int f$$ with $$C = 0$$ over the given interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack.$$ Approximate a value of C, if possible, such that adding C to the antiderivative gives the same value as the definite integral $$F(x) = {\int_{a}^{x}{f(t)dt.}}$$

solution.paragraph: The antiderivative is $$12sec-1(x2)+C.12sec-1(x2)+C.$$ Taking $$C=0C=0$$ recovers the definite integral over $$[2,6].[2,6].$$
The general antiderivative is $$tan-1(xsinx)+C.tan-1(xsinx)+C.$$ Taking $$C=-tan-1(6sin(6))C=-tan-1(6sin(6))$$ recovers the definite integral.
The general antiderivative is $$tan-1(lnx)+C.tan-1(lnx)+C.$$ Taking $$C=\pi 2=tan-1\infty C=\pi 2=tan-1\infty$$ recovers the definite integral.

Use the substitution $$u = \sqrt{2} \cot x$$ and the identity $$1 + \cot^{2}x = \csc^{2}x$$ to evaluate $$\left. \int{\frac{dx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}.} \right.$$ (Hint: Multiply the top and bottom of the integrand by $$\csc^{2}x.)$$

solution.paragraph: Using the hint, one has $$\int csc2xcsc2x+cot2xdx=\int csc2x1+2cot2xdx.\int csc2xcsc2x+cot2xdx=\int csc2x1+2cot2xdx.$$ Set $$u=2cotx.u=2cotx.$$ Then, $$du=-2csc2xdu=-2csc2x$$ and the integral is $$-12\int du1+u2=-12tan-1u+C=12tan-1(2cotx)+C.-12\int du1+u2=-12tan-1u+C=12tan-1(2cotx)+C.$$ If one uses the identity $$tan-1s+tan-1(1s)=\pi 2,tan-1s+tan-1(1s)=\pi 2,$$ then this can also be written $$12tan-1(tanx2)+C.12tan-1(tanx2)+C.$$
